headline: The 15800 least-volume cuttings of the unit four-cube at the adjacency cost floor draw on 192 pieces, 24 pieces to a cutting, each piece lying on 1975 cuttings, and 192 sets of eight pieces each meet every cutting exactly once. Earlier cycles measured the space of piece vectors that every cutting sums to zero at 104 dimensions and identified it with the span of the differences of those 192 covers, but every one of those statements is a statement over the rationals, while the pieces carry whole-number labellings. This cycle asks the whole-number question. Off the diagonal two covers share 0, 1, 2 or 4 pieces with counts 30144, 3840, 1920 and 768, so each cover shares 0 pieces with 157 of the others, 1 with 20, 2 with 10 and 4 with 4, which takes in all 191; since two covers sharing s pieces differ on twice the 8 less s they do not share, the largest sharing 4 gives the smallest difference, supported on 8 pieces with entries -1 0 1, and there are 384 of them, every one sent to zero by the cutting table. The finding is that these 384 smallest exchanges do not merely span the blind space over the rationals: 104 of them are a whole-number basis of the blind lattice, so every whole-number blind labelling is a whole-number combination of four-for-four exchanges, and the 191 differences from one fixed cover already suffice. The instrument is the determinantal divisor: for a matrix of rank r the greatest common divisor of all r by r minors is the product of the invariant factors, so a single minor of absolute value 1 forces every invariant factor to 1, hence saturation of the row lattice, rank r in every characteristic, and a quotient free of torsion. Two minors from opposite column orders are computed at each rank and both come out 1: 88 by 88 for the cutting table, 105 by 105 for the cover table, 104 by 104 for the smallest exchanges and again for the single-cover differences. Saturation is the lever, since two saturated lattices of the same rank with one inside the other are equal. The two table ranks are therefore 88 and 105 over every field, confirmed directly over 13 primes with a second scalar routine reproducing 105 and a fixed control dropping to 0, 1 and 3. The counterweight is that the split is not integral: the lattice the cuttings measure, rank 88, and the blind lattice, rank 104, are orthogonal complements over the rationals but glue inside the whole-number labellings at index 2^114 x 3 x 5^30, established three ways that must agree and from two independent choices of basis. The finite group that index counts is measured from three matrices of three different sizes, the 88 by 88 measured inner product, the 104 by 104 blind inner product and the 192 by 192 stacked basis, and all three return the same group: 42 cyclic parts of orders 2, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320 and 960 with multiplicities 12, 8, 2, 2, 8, 8, 1 and 1. Their orders divide one another in turn and their product is exactly the index measured separately, so the exponent is 960, which is 5 times the 192 pieces, the smallest whole number carrying every piece labelling into a whole-number measured part plus a whole-number blind part. Controls fixed in advance: the determinant routine returns 0, 144 and 1 on fixed inputs and the witness reports 144 rather than 1 on a diagonal whose invariant factors are not all one; the invariant-factor routine returns 2 and 2 6 12 unchanged but returns 1 6 and 2 12 from the diagonals 2 3 and 4 6, so it is not reading off the entries it was handed; and a pair of lattices in the integer plane whose gluing index is 2 by hand returns 2 from all three routes. Left open: whether any blind vector has support below 8, why the index takes the value it does, and whether the 42 cyclic parts answer to a decomposition of the 192 cover directions.
